'applied': the text, generator or check script was changed as described in 'note'; 'applied in part': the defect was fixed but part of the suggested fix was not used, for the reason given. Every changed number was recomputed from the sources named in the note.

problems.file: sections/abstract.tex (and tables/tab_headline.tex via make_tables.py tab_headline; contradicts sections/results.tex)
problems.location: abstract, 'Over 126 in-sample targets it is -1.87'; tab:headline row 'pooled: 126 targets of 10 suites', limits column 'in-sample'
problems.problem: The 126 targets are the 10 suites with network runs INCLUDING the held-out dlheld7 (12 targets), as results.tex sec:res-suites and tab:pooled state. So 12 of the 126 are held out, and calling the pooled -1.87 an 'in-sample' number is wrong. Recomputed from the result files: over the 114 in-sample targets (9 suites without dlheld7) the mean is -1.93 over the 112 both learn (median -1.69; 107 clearly better, 2 clearly worse).
problems.fix: Write 'Over all 126 targets with network runs (114 in-sample, plus dlheld7) it is -1.87', or quote the in-sample pool (-1.93 over 112 of 114). In tab:headline say 'in-sample except dlheld7's 12' (or recompute the row without dlheld7).
problems.note: abstract: 'Over the 114 in-sample targets with network runs it is -1.93' (recomputed from RESULTS.json q2_suites per-target ratios without dlheld7: 112 both learn, median -1.69, 107 clearly better, 2 worse; make_tables.py tab_headline now computes it, numbers.json tab_headline.pooled_in_sample). tab:headline limits: 'in-sample except dlheld7's 12; the 114 in-sample targets alone: -1.93 over 112'. results.tex Pooled bullet adds the in-sample pool.

problems.location: sec:res-dscale, Results bullet 'Same as Part 6's DFG'
problems.problem: 'DFG v1.3 gives the n* of Part 6's DFG ... the median log2 difference is 0.00 at every d' overstates the agreement. (i) tab:dscale prints -0.01 at d=30 (RESULTS.json q4_dscale.per_d.30.dfg_vs_part6.median = -0.0054), so the text contradicts its own table. (ii) 6 of the 25 (target, d) cells differ by more than the 0.25 tie band: maj9 at d=30 (81 vs 107, -0.40), d=60 (167 vs 227, -0.44) and d=120 (104 vs 439, -2.08); par3 at d=30 (28 vs 16, +0.80); par4 at d=15 (28 vs 16, +0.80) and d=30 (52 vs 21, +1.28). Only the medians agree. Part 6 also ran in the natural column order, which can favour it on parities at tiny n.
problems.fix: Change the heading to 'Close to Part 6's DFG in median' and write: 'the median log2 difference is between -0.01 and 0.00 at every d, but 6 of 25 (target, d) cells differ by more than 0.25: v1.3 is faster on maj9 at d>=30 (up to 104 vs 439 at d=120) and slower on par3 and par4 at d<=30, where Part 6 saw the inputs in their natural order.'
problems.note: results.tex: heading 'Close to Part 6's DFG in median'; median between -0.01 and 0.00; 6 of the 25 (target, d) cells beyond 0.25 (maj9 faster at d>=30, up to 104 vs 439; par3 at d=30 and par4 at d=15, 30 slower, natural column order). The cell list is computed by make_tables.py (numbers.json tab_dscale.dfg_vs_part6_beyond_tie).

problems.location: sec:res-lowdeg, Reading (Heuristic), first and fifth sentences
problems.problem: 'DFG alone's margin over the networks does not come from its dictionary or its test' and 'The sum blocks make the signed-sum targets learnable at all' are stronger than the data. lowdeg learns 39 of the 54 sum-structured targets, just more slowly: it never learns 15 of them, and DFG alone also misses 4 of those 15. DFG without sum blocks (nosums, RESULTS.json q5_ablations) is newly 'never' on only 3 of the 65 ablation targets (band11, h6_01, f7_08). The data show that dictionary plus test are not sufficient. They do not show that these parts contribute nothing, and the sum blocks mostly make sum targets cheaper, not possible.
problems.fix: 'DFG alone's margin over the networks is not explained by its dictionary and test alone' and 'The sum blocks make the signed-sum targets much cheaper to learn (nosums: +0.91 mean log2 n*), and a few learnable at all within the grid (band11, h6_01, f7_08)'.
problems.note: results.tex lowdeg Reading: 'is not explained by its dictionary and test alone'; the sum blocks make sum targets 'much cheaper to learn, and a few learnable at all within the grid' (lowdeg learns 39 of the 54 sum-structured targets, numbers.json tab_lowdeg.sum_structured; nosums +0.91 and newly never on band11, h6_01, f7_08).

problems.location: sec:res-dlheld7: paragraph heading 'Five of the ten wins need no feature search [Numerical]' and the following Reading ('the other five, the sum-structured ones')
problems.problem: (i) The heading is a conclusion, not a measurement: what is measured is that a calibration reference is clearly better than nets_best on 5 targets, while DFG alone is clearly worse than hgb on 2 of them (f7_02, f7_06). (ii) 'the other five, the sum-structured ones' implies the five calibration wins are not sum-structured. But f7_10 (a composite sum) and f7_11 (a multiplexer between two signed sums) are sum-structured by protocol.tex's own definition, which counts all 9 non-control dlheld7 targets among the 54 sum-structured targets. The Reading also calls f7_11 a 'small formula'.
problems.fix: Heading: 'On five of the ten wins a calibration reference also beats the networks'. Reading: 'the other five, where no calibration reference is competitive (all sum-structured)'. Call f7_11 a multiplexer of two sums.
problems.note: results.tex: heading 'On five of the ten wins a calibration reference also beats the networks'; Reading: 'the other five wins, where no calibration reference is competitive (all five are sum-structured)'; f7_11 called a multiplexer of two sums.

problems.file: sections/protocol.tex (also used in results.tex sec:res-dlheld7 and intro.tex)
problems.location: sec:refs, Calibration references: 'They search no features, so they show which targets need none'
problems.problem: hgb is histogram gradient boosting. It greedily grows trees whose leaves are conjunctions of input literals, which is itself a feature search, and Part 7 (STANDARD-TASKS.md) calls gradient boosting 'a discrete, greedily grown learner too'. The results build on this framing: 'need no feature search', 'no learner without feature search comes close'.
problems.fix: 'They search no explicit feature dictionary (lin none at all, hgb only through greedy splits on single inputs), so they show which targets need no dictionary search'. Adjust the dependent phrases in results.tex and intro.tex.
problems.note: protocol.tex: 'Neither searches an explicit feature dictionary: lin searches no features at all, and hgb only through greedy splits on single inputs. So they show which targets need no dictionary search.' Dependent phrases in results.tex, intro.tex and discussion.tex now say 'calibration reference' / 'neither calibration reference comes close'.

problems.note: results.tex Reading: 'On h3rf1, and on the ties h3rf0 and and3, DFG's lack of a clear margin reflects its slowness at small n ...'.

problems.location: sec:res-v3, paragraph 'Why', counts at n=16, 32, 64
problems.problem: 'v3's error is lower than its own DFG member's by more than 0.02 in 57, 68 and 53 fits'. In the 52, 47 and 30 fits where the stacker gave DFG no weight, the 'member' is v3's last out-of-fold DFG fit (on 15 or 29 rows at n=16/32), not a fit on all n rows. This caveat is only in the caption of tab:v3-byn, so the text overstates how often v3 beats a comparable DFG fit at small n.
problems.fix: Add the caveat in the text ('where the stacker gave DFG no weight, the member is its last out-of-fold fit on fewer rows'), or also give the counts over the fits that have a final DFG member.
problems.note: results.tex Why: caveat added with recomputed out-of-fold row counts (13-15, 28-30 and 57-58 rows at n=16, 32, 64; the checker's '15 or 29' was approximate) and the counts over the fits with a final DFG member (86, 91, 106 fits; v3 lower in 29, 45, 33; higher in 16, 9, 10), which are now also three rows of tab:v3-byn(b), computed by make_tables.py from the Part 10 refit files (dfg_source field).

problems.location: sec:res-v3, Why, Reading: 'Once DFG's features pass their tests, its members take most of the weight and the two learners agree'
problems.problem: tab:v3-byn(b): the median DFG weight share is 0.73-0.81 at n=256-1024, but 0.64, 0.51, 0.19 and 0.15 at n=2048, 4096, 8192 and 16384 (33, 16, 10 and 7 fits). At the largest n the DFG members do not take most of the weight; the errors agree because all members are near 0.
problems.fix: 'At n=256-2048 its members take most of the weight (median 0.64-0.81) and the two learners agree; at larger n, where few analysed fits remain and every member is near 0 error, the stacker spreads its weight.'
problems.note: Overclaim fixed: 'at n=256-2048 its members take most of the weight (median share 0.64-0.81)'. The checker's explanation for larger n ('every member is near 0 error') was not used, because the refit files show otherwise: the 16, 10 and 7 fits left at n=4096-16384 are mostly targets no member fits (fd_10, h6_00, f7_05, h5s1, and h5s7 at 4096; errors 0.32-0.50) and the dense halfspaces thr20 and thr30, on which logistic regression takes most of the weight. The text says this (numbers.json tab_v3.inside_v3_large_n).

problems.location: fig:dscale caption, 'Refits of the stored fits show two exceptions ... And par4 at d=30 (n_thr=30.6) passed at n=32 in 1 of 3 seeds'
problems.problem: This is not an exception to the criterion the caption states (n(1-ybar^2) > n_thr). It is what that criterion predicts.
